exposure: Group psychoeducation with relaxation (six sessions during pregnancy, one after childbirth)
Conventional care (surveillance and referral on demand)
outcome: All costs in maternity care during pregnancy, delivery and postnatally
cohort: A total of 371 nulliparous women scoring over the 95th centile in the Wijma Delivery Expectancy Questionnaire (W-DEQ) during their first trimester were included.
finding: The psychoeducation and conventional care groups showed no significant differences in total direct costs, life satisfaction, or general well-being, but the psychoeducation group had a higher rate of uncomplicated vaginal deliveries for the same overall costs.
mod_finding: The psychoeducation group experienced a significantly greater number of uncomplicated vaginal deliveries (63%) compared to the conventional care group (47%).
